query: For high-entropy-alloy coatings used in wear-resistant applications, what single intervention could improve wear resistance across operating temperatures? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its expected mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise identical unmodified coating, the temperature and sliding conditions under which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of silver (Ag) to high-entropy alloy coatings improves wear resistance across operating temperatures.
generation.intervention: Addition of silver (Ag) to the high-entropy alloy coatings
generation.conditions: Operating temperatures ranging from room temperature to high temperatures (up to 750 °C), dry sliding wear conditions
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a lubricious film consisting of Ag and various oxides on the frictional surface
generation.mechanism: The lubricious film contributes to low friction and wear, improving wear resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance of the high-entropy alloy coatings with silver across operating temperatures
generation.baseline: Wear resistance of high-entropy alloy coatings without silver
generation.boundary: Operating temperatures and dry sliding wear conditions
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of silver to be added and the specific high-entropy alloy composition that would benefit most from the addition of silver

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of wear resistance of high-entropy alloy coatings with and without silver under various operating temperatures and dry sliding wear conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear resistance of high-entropy alloy coatings with silver is not significantly improved compared to those without silver, the hypothesis is falsified

Question: How does the addition of Silver (Ag) and the variation in temperature affect the tribological properties and wear mechanisms of plasma-sprayed Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti-based high-entropy coatings?. System: Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti-Ag (HEA-Ag) and Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti (HEC) coatings formed on carbon steel. Processing: Plasma spraying. Test conditions: Temperature range from 25 to 750 °C; ball-on-disk sliding; counterface not explicitly named in the specific Li et al. summary but implied standard tribological testing. Paper card. Question: How does grain size influence the tribological behavior, wear mechanisms, and wear resistance of CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloys under varying normal loads and sliding speeds?. System: CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy (HEA) with fine grain (FG, ~2.9 μm) and coarse grain (CG, ~63.4 μm) microstructures. Processing: Arc-melting of pure metals followed by drop-casting into a copper mold, forging at 1000 °C, cold rolling (80% reduction), and annealing at 800 °C for 30 min (FG) or 1000 °C for 60 min (CG). Test conditions: Reciprocating sliding friction against a 10 mm Si3N4 ball under dry conditions at room temperature; normal loads of 5 N and 30 N; sliding speeds of 1, 5, and 10 mm/s; sliding time of 1200 s.
